Salvage law developed differently from ordinary property law because the circumstances were different: a ship in distress cannot negotiate, and a rescuer who bargains hard is close to extortion. The compromise that emerged rewards successful salvage generously and unsuccessful attempts not at all, which aligns the incentive with the outcome anybody actually wants. It is one of the few areas where an obviously artificial rule survives because the natural one produces worse behaviour.

Typefaces designed for road signs are optimised for a reading situation almost nobody else faces: a glance, at distance, at speed, often in poor light, by someone who must then act. The resulting letterforms look clumsy on a page and are highly legible on a gantry. It is a good illustration of how a design brief that specifies the reading conditions produces something quite unlike a design brief that specifies beauty.

The domestication of the horse changed the effective size of political units, because the distance a message could travel in a day set the limit on how much territory could be governed as one thing. Empires expanded to roughly the radius that their communications allowed and then became unstable beyond it. The pattern recurs with every subsequent change in transmission speed, and the boundaries move without the underlying constraint being noticed.

Tide prediction was one of the earliest problems attacked with mechanical computation, because the answer is a sum of periodic components whose frequencies are known and whose amplitudes vary by location. Machines built from pulleys and cams could add those components far faster than a clerk, and the results were accurate enough to publish. The method preceded any complete theory of the tides, which mattered less than it might because the components could be measured directly.

Assaying exists because metal cannot be trusted by appearance, and the history of coinage is largely a history of attempts to make debasement detectable. Milled edges, standardised weights and hallmarks are all answers to the same problem: how to let a stranger verify a claim cheaply. Each answer worked until forgery caught up with it, at which point the verification moved to a property that was harder to imitate than to check.

Grafting is an old technique that produces something genetically peculiar: a single plant with two distinct sets of tissue, roots chosen for hardiness and a crown chosen for fruit. Most orchard varieties cannot be grown true from seed, so every tree of a named apple is in some sense a cutting of one original. The practice preserves individuals rather than lineages, which is an unusual thing for agriculture to do.

Weather forecasting became reliable not when the physics was understood but when the observations became dense and fast enough to initialise it. The equations had been written down long before there was any way to know the current state of the atmosphere at sufficient resolution, and a perfect model of a poorly known present is not much use. Forecast skill improved with telegraphy, then with radiosondes, then with satellites, each time for the same reason.

The idea of a fire break is that the cheapest way to stop a spreading process is to remove what it feeds on, ahead of it, rather than to fight it where it is. The same logic reappears in epidemiology, in firewalls, and in the design of ship compartments. What makes it hard in practice is that the break must be made before the threat arrives, in a place that may turn out not to have needed it.

Standardised shipping containers are usually credited with reducing freight cost, which they did, but the larger effect was on the ports. Break-bulk cargo required large workforces near the water; containers required cranes and land. Ports therefore moved out of cities to places with space, and the districts they left behind spent decades finding another use. The technology changed the map more than the price list.

Latitude could be found from the sun with modest instruments; longitude required knowing the time somewhere else, and that turned a problem of astronomy into a problem of engineering. Clocks that kept time on land failed at sea, defeated by motion, temperature and humidity. The eventual solution was mechanical rather than celestial, which disappointed a scientific establishment that had expected the answer to come from the sky.

Beekeeping is unusual among animal husbandries in that the animals are not confined and could leave at any time. Management consists largely of arranging conditions the colony prefers to those available elsewhere, and of removing surplus without provoking abandonment. The relationship is closer to tenancy than ownership, and the vocabulary of the craft reflects an old awareness of that.

Public clocks preceded personal watches by centuries, and for most of that time the correct time was a civic fact rather than a private one. A town had a time, announced by a bell, and disagreement with it was simply error. Portable timepieces made time something individuals could hold and therefore something they could disagree about, which is why synchronisation became a subject at all.

Waterproofing fabric is a compromise, because a coating that excludes liquid water usually also traps vapour, and a wearer generating heat will end up wet from the inside. The interesting materials are the ones that discriminate by molecule size or by pressure gradient rather than simply sealing. Every solution trades durability against breathability, and the marketing is generally about whichever side the product wins.

Anonymous manuscripts are dated by evidence their authors never intended to leave: the ruling of the page, the abbreviation habits of the scribe, the chemistry of the ink, the provenance of the parchment. None of it is the content, and all of it is more reliable than the content, which can be copied from an older exemplar. The method is a reminder that a document has a physical history distinct from its text.

Dry stone walls hold together by friction and geometry rather than mortar, which makes them repairable by anyone who understands the principle and unrepairable by anyone who does not. They also drain and flex, so they survive ground movement that would crack a rigid wall. The technique persists in upland farming not from conservatism but because the alternative performs worse in that particular setting.

The transition from oral to written law changed what law was, because a written rule can be consulted by people who were not present when it was made and cannot be adjusted quietly in the telling. Codification therefore tends to accompany expansions of the governed population, and it reliably produces a new profession whose expertise is in what the text says as against what everyone assumed it said.

Lens grinding limited astronomy for a long period, because the useful aperture was bounded by what could be made without sagging or chromatic error. Mirrors sidestepped part of the problem and introduced others, notably the difficulty of a stable figure and a reflective coating that did not tarnish. Each advance in optics opened a band of objects that had been present all along and unobservable in practice.
